Aeolus Microtexts

Source: CONTEXT.md

Analyses the microtexts of the Aeolus episode of Ulysses as if they were social media content, using LLM-based qualitative coding across three research questions.

Language

Research question (RQ): One of three fixed lines of inquiry (RQ1 sentiment, RQ2 nationalism, RQ3 UGC-resemblance). Each RQ has a fixed RQ schema that does not vary across a run. Avoid: rq, question, analysis type

Context variant: One of three framings prepended to the system prompt, giving the LLM different background about the text before it: no_context, ulysses_context (“this text is from Ulysses”), media_text_context (“this text is/is intended to be media text”). Crossed independently within each research question. Avoid: prompt variant, framing, condition

RQ schema: The fixed coding schema of a research question, holding both its task instruction and the definitions of its output fields. The single source of truth for what the model is asked to do and for the output shape enforced during generation. Enforcement constrains structure only; the model reads nothing of the RQ schema except what is rendered into the system prompt. Avoid: coding schema, response format, type

Task instruction: The sentence(s) telling the model what to classify for a given research question. Derived programmatically from the RQ schema, not hand-duplicated. Avoid: system prompt (system prompt = context variant + task instruction + output specification)

Output specification: The plain-text rendering of the RQ schema’s output fields (name, meaning, allowed values or type, in schema order) included in the system prompt, so the model reads what each field means rather than only having its structure enforced. Avoid: response format (collides with the API request field that carries the enforced schema), RQ schema (the source, not its rendering)

System prompt: Context variant + task instruction + output specification, fixed within a grid cell. The unit of analysis is sent separately as the user turn, under a “The text” heading (results CSVs record the bare unit, without the heading). Avoid: prompt (ambiguous: system prompt or user turn)

Unit of analysis: The span of text a single LLM call classifies. Defined by two orthogonal factors: granularity (microtext vs sentence) and include_headline (whether the ALL-CAPS headline is included — prepended to the unit at microtext granularity, or retained as its own unit rather than filtered out at sentence granularity). Its concrete text is recorded in a results CSV’s unit_of_analysis column; see docs/adr/0003-results-csv-schema.md for the full row schema. Avoid: chunk, segment

Microtext: A block of text in 7_Aeolus.txt delimited by an ALL-CAPS headline, treated as the analogue of a single social-media post. Identified in results CSVs by the microtext column (an integer id); the R-internal grouping variable is still called section. Avoid: post, entry, section (post is fine informally, but microtext is the canonical term)

Grid cell: One combination of research question × model × context variant × unit of analysis — the atomic unit of work in a run, corresponding to one (or more, for sentence granularity) LLM classification calls. Every row in a results CSV carries an explicit column for each of these factors, so rows/files are self-describing and freely concatenable regardless of how the run happened to be split across files; see docs/adr/0003-results-csv-schema.md. Avoid: combination, run, condition

Run: One invocation of the pipeline across some or all of the grid, identified by a run_id combining a timestamp and the installed aeolusmicrotexts package version (e.g. 20260821-153000_v0.1.0.9000), so output is traceable to the exact code that produced it. Lives only in the results/<run_id>/... directory/filename layer (docs/adr/0003-results-csv-schema.md), never as its own CSV column; see docs/adr/0004-install-package-for-targets-workers.md for why the version is embedded. Avoid: sweep (used informally elsewhere for the same concept, but “run” is the canonical term)

Promoted run: A run whose results and model digests were manually copied into inst/extdata/results/<run_id>/ after researcher review, and so readable from the installed package. Avoid: sweep, published run

Test mode: A single R parameter that switches the pipeline to a reduced sweep for local/Docker validation: 5 microtexts, using only the small llama3.2:1b model. Controlled entirely in R, not via targets branching. Avoid: dev mode, dry run

Dispatcher job: The single SLURM job (submitted by scripts/test-run.sh/scripts/run-sweep.sh, non-GPU, sapphire partition) that runs targets::tar_make() itself: builds the grid, pulls every model into its model store once before any worker starts, and coordinates workers, but does no LLM inference. Exists to get tar_make() off the login node (compute nodes can’t dial back into a login-node-hosted crew socket; see docs/adr/0001-crew-cluster-drives-slurm.md). Submitted fire-and-forget (no --wait) — the submitting script returns as soon as sbatch accepts the job, it does not block until the run finishes. Avoid: tar_make job, controller job, orchestrator (dispatcher is the canonical term, paired with “worker” below)

Worker: A crew.cluster SLURM job (one per model, GPU partition, per slurm-resources.yml) that runs ollama serve, checks that its model is already present in its model store (never pulls it — the dispatcher job does), and then executes grid cells dispatched to it. Launched and torn down by the dispatcher job, not submitted directly by any script. Avoid: node, task runner (worker is the crew-native term, kept as-is here)

Model store: The project’s own directory (a sibling of the repo checkout) that every Ollama server in a run reads models from, and that the dispatcher job pulls into. Shared by every run, so only one run may be active at a time — a run starting up can delete a concurrent run’s in-progress pull. Avoid: pull-cache, models dir, shared model directory, central store (the cluster-wide store, no longer used)

Chat backend: An injectable argument (default ellmer::chat_ollama) threaded through the analysis functions, swappable for a mocked/fake implementation in fast logic tests. Exists because ellmer has no built-in mock/test chat provider. Avoid: LLM client, provider (backend is the pipeline-specific term)
